short_description: The largest-diameter, fastest, most purely glycolytic fibre in human skeletal muscle: a single, unbranched, cylindrical cell centimetres long (~30 mm) and ~70 um across, cross-striated along its whole length, with many flattened nuclei just under the sarcolemma at the periphery (never one central nucleus), sparse mitochondria, a thin capillary supply and abundant glycogen granules, pale pink-cream rather than red because it carries little myoglobin. Recruited last, only for maximal effort, and fatigues within seconds. What older histochemistry called human 'Type IIb' is this fibre under a different name -- true MYH4-expressing IIb is a rodent fibre, essentially absent from adult human limb muscle.
